7464 A Comparative Study of Clustering Stock Prices Using K-Means and Fuzzy C-Means Algorithms
Authors: Abhijit K. Behera, Rajashree Behera
Abstract:
Cluster analysis has been widely used in the financial industry to group stocks with similar characteristics using different valuation criteria. It helps investors to make vital decisions in money management, portfolio diversification, and hedging by identifying stocks with price similarities to find profitable investment opportunities. In this paper, we make a comparison of K-means and Fuzzy C-means algorithms for clustering analysis of the stock prices in the financial market. For illustrative purposes, the daily closing prices of the stocks traded on the National Stock Exchange (NSE) of India during the financial year 2013-14 are considered and using the K-means and Fuzzy C-means algorithms, they are categorized into five different groups. The proposed clustering algorithms are validated using suitable validation indexes.

11.00 - 12.00
Distributed Deep Reinforcement Learning to Improve Internet-of-Things Security and Trust
By:
Yingfei Dong, University of Alabama, Tuscaloosa, USA
Abstract:
Traditional security and privacy approaches have focused on a centralized architecture, in which a single entity acts as a central authority (or service provider) for decision making and executing security and privacy protection operations. Although this approach works well with the conventional Internet system, it does not fit well with the requirements for the emerging Internet-of-Things (IoT) where devices and users operate in a highly distributed and dynamic environment.
In this talk, I will first introduce a novel security and privacy framework called DisSEPT (Distributed SecuRity and PriVacy Trust) for distributed IoT networks. The DisSEPT framework includes a novel user/device trust modeling approach using blockchain technology, an efficient reputation and trust computation method, a flexible security and privacy policy management approach, and a dynamic security strategy distribution protocol.
Next, I will present a deep reinforcement learning (RL)-based security and privacy defense framework for IoT network, called DisDLT. The DisDLT framework is able to learn optimal decisions and policies in the presence of attacks. The proposed DisDLT framework uses a novel distributed learning algorithm based on deep RL techniques to train a reinforcement learning agent to learn and adapt to the network attacks. We further propose an adaptive strategy to learn both short-term and long-term attack responses.

Abstract:
In this study, two-dimensional wave tank is simulated based on the finite difference method using Reynolds averaged Navier- Stokes equation for turbulent motion of the fluid under consideration. In this regard, SST k -ω turbulence model is used in the modeling for better prediction of the shear and the near wall flow. An iterative solution is applied to simulate the two-dimensional wave tank until the results converge in the desired range. The simulation results are validated by the experimental results given by RIA, Japan. Results show that the good agreements of the simulated results with the desired data is obtained. After validation of the simulated model, the wave tank is simulated with different wave heights and wave periods for a fixed water depth of 1.5 meters in order to study the dependency of the velocity and the pressure fields in the tank to these parameters. Results indicate that the pressure in the tank has a linear increase with the increase of the wave height, while the increasing trend is not linear for the velocity field.

Three subjects were measured with a Hartinger coincidence interferometer, and two subjects were measured with an Alvarez interferometer. Dark focus was measured for several luminances with a 3° diameter target under each attention task. Subjects viewed a 5 min of fixation and 1 min of tracking under low luminance (2 × 10−3 cd/m2). Interindividual dark-focus values for the low luminance condition (r = 0.755, n = 3, p = .105) and high luminance condition (r = 0.999, n = 2, p < .01) both reached a high level of significance.
Results:
In all cases, subjects’ dark focus shifted in the direction of the accommodation target. Under dark conditions, subjects averaged −0.45 D to −1.02 D. During a closed-loop tracking task, subjects’ dark focuses were on average −1.59 D to −3.33 D. In each subject, dark focus values under dark conditions (low luminance) correlated significantly with dark focus values during the visual tracking task (high luminance). This suggests that dark focus and visual attention are associated.
Conclusions:
It was found that accommodation varies more from person to person than had been previously reported. Accommodation under low luminance is different from accommodation measured with the classical dark room protocol, but a high level of correlation exists between accommodation under low luminance and during closed-loop tracking.

Aims & objectives: To study the feasibility of AMM in routine practice from a developing country.
Methods: We conducted a retrospective review of patients diagnosed with ICAD at our institute between January 2012 and June 2015. We collected information on demographic data, medical and neurological history, clinical presentation, presence and degree of ICAD on CT/DSA/MRA, initial medical management (including medication used) and follow-up information. Our primary outcome measures were in-stent restenosis (ISR), symptomatic stroke, and death. Secondary outcome was a composite of any of the following: symptomatic stroke, transient ischemic attack (TIA), and mortality.
Results: A total of 35 patients were included in the study. All patients received clopidogrel and a statin. In addition, 32 patients received dual antiplatelet therapy (DAPT) (clopidogrel + aspirin), for an average duration of 101±118 days. Mean follow-up was 246±157 days. None of our patients received a stent, and none developed ISR. There was one mortality (2.85%) at 162 days of follow up and two patients (5.71%) developed symptomatic stroke (one had an ipsilateral stroke and the other developed contralateral TIA) at a median follow up of 12 months. 85% (30/35) of patients achieved target LDL-C level. Overall, we achieved 91% (32/35) success rate in treating symptomatic ICAD with AMM.
Conclusions: AMM, with the use of DAPT, high dose statin and tight LDL-C control, appears to be safe and effective in the routine clinical setting in India. This approach should be studied further to determine its role in the management
